title: Tries
subtitle: A trie shares common key prefixes so each traversed edge refines the set of possible completions.
variables: L = query/key length in Python Unicode code points; Lmax = maximum dictionary key length (0 for no nonempty keys); k = requested suggestion count; T = total dictionary input size, sum(len(word)+1) over supplied key occurrences (so empty and duplicate keys count); P = number of allocated prefix nodes (P ≤ T+1 for an ordinary character trie); A = alphabet size; N = number of supplied keys/values, including duplicates; M = text length; B = chosen integer bit width; Z = total characters in returned output; R*C = board cells. Dictionary-backed child transitions are expected O(1); whole-string hashing/comparison costs O(L) initially/worst-case and substring creation is not free. Complexity uses a bounded-word arithmetic model; Python arbitrary-sized integers and normalization have additional costs. Trie storage is O(P) dictionary entries/nodes, but Python per-node constants are substantial. Auxiliary space includes explicit stacks/recursion and excludes separately stated output; operations that create stored nodes identify persistent growth. All templates are standard-library Python 3.10+, iterative at unbounded input depth.
